question: As of 1 February 2026, the Government of the Kingdom of Morocco has suspended the export of frozen sardines for at least one year. Given that Morocco is a key supplier of sardines to the European Union and that Member States such as Spain, Portugal and Italy are heavily dependent on them for their canning industries: 1.

Does the Commission intend to activate the consultation mechanisms under the EUMorocco Association Agreement to assess whether this unilateral restriction complies with the Moroccan authorities’ trade cooperation obligations?
What contingency or compensation measures does the Commission plan to adopt to prevent stock shortages in the EU canning industry?
How does the Commission intend to safeguard the economic interests of Member States now facing high prices to acquire this raw material?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.3.2026) The Commission is aware of the issue regarding the exports of sardines from Morocco. At this stage, the Commission services and the Delegation of the EU to Morocco are investigating, and will assess how best to tackle the issue. In the meantime, alternative sources of supply from preferential partner countries exist via a large network of EU Free Trade Agreements.
There is also supply from the EU vessels fishing in the EU waters and the EU production can be used to supply the EU canneries.
